name: P6 drop cue separability (feasibility, not a detector pass)
status: PROPOSAL — NOT APPROVED. Host research only.
question: Does any causal feature on the Titan's audio stream put every drop above everything else? Feasibility comes before design (PL14 C15/C16).
stream: The v4 windows from runs/P6-DROP-DETECTOR/v4/detector.py load_scored_windows: 24 kHz, 180-sample hops (7.5 ms), the two source files, the two room recordings and the seen Carte file. A feature value at a hop may use only that hop and earlier samples.

features.F1_sub_vs_median: 30–110 Hz causal Butterworth order 2 band, 10 ms causal mean-square level (dB), minus its median over the previous 1.0 s ending 50 ms before the hop.
features.F2_sub_vs_max: The same level minus its maximum over the previous 1.0 s ending 50 ms before the hop.
features.F5_sub_vs_p90_2s: The sub level minus its 90th percentile over the previous 2.0 s ending 50 ms before the hop.

drop_value: For each required drop, the maximum feature value over hops whose end lies in [anchor, anchor + 0.050] s song time.
non_drop_value: The maximum feature value over every scored hop more than 0.5 s from every drop, on every window. Hops in the first 2.0 s of a window are not scored (trailing statistics need history).
feasible: A feature is feasible when min(drop values over all six required drops) - max(non-drop values over all five windows) >= 3.0 dB. Every window counts; Carte is seen, not a holdout.
infeasible: If no feature reaches the 3.0 dB margin, the report names the drop and the non-drop hop that close the gap.

planted_faults.anchor_shift_minus_100ms: Re-run the best feature with every anchor moved 100 ms earlier (the hit window then lies in the build). Expected RED: its margin falls below 3.0 dB.
planted_faults.shuffled_anchor: Re-run the best feature with each window's anchor replaced by the time 10.0 s earlier. Expected RED.
